articleTitle: Mechatronics Design of High-Altitude Balloon Paulet-1 for Peruvian Aerospace Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: This research has been implemented with a focus on the optimal mechatronics resources for Aerospace Monitoring in Peruvian Sky, specifically on the Troposphere. The device is called Paulet-1, which is a prototype developed in the Mechatronics Laboratory at Ricardo Palma University, Peru from 2017 to 2018. The design consisted of the analysis of the size, weight and price in order to create a sustainable embedded system to measure variables of humidity, pressure, temperature and localization, besides, the development was based on the technological risk caused by the earth’s atmosphere conditions. The Tests were performed in 3 locations, the First was in Santiago de Surco District, the Second was in Lurín District and the Third was in Asia District, all were in Lima Province. In conclusion, favorable results were achieved; therefore, the next version of the prototype Paultet-2 is confirmed to be ready for developing in 2020.

articleTitle: Building a Text Messaging-Based System to Support Low-Cost Automation in Household Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: Home garden crops, small-scale agricultural systems for local food production, are becoming an integral part of the food supply chain in a number of developing countries and peri-urban areas of some developed regions. In this work, we propose a low-cost, monitoring and irrigation system which can be applied in household and local community gardens. The basic architecture consists of a sensing/actuation station based on commercial off-the-shelf hardware and a mobile application for the interaction with remote users. A key aspect of the system is the use of legacy text-messaging service as a mechanism to support alert and control operations for monitoring and irrigation. This feature enables widely available and highly-reliable connections between the cropland station and remote users without the need for new network infrastructure. We implemented a functional prototype of the system to check its effectivity in a small open-field area for tomatoes cultivation. The results show that water usage can be substantially improved if using both the actual information collected from the system and public tools for decision support in agriculture. We conclude that the proposed solution has a good prospect as an input for the design of more automated decision-strategies to be used in plant cultivation of a similar kind and/or of a larger scale.

articleTitle: Weighting Factor Selection in Power Converters Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) lacks of theoretical or numerical methods to adjust the weighting factors within the cost function. This research proposes a methodology to improve the selection of weighting factors in power converters based on MPC. A Multi-Objective MPC was implemented in Neutral Point Clamped Inverter to demonstrate the strategy and the influence of each term in the cost function equation. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology could be demonstrated, as well as the advantages of using MPC with multiple control objectives. However, efforts are needed to improve the weight factor selection process, especially if multiple control variables are added to the cost function.

articleTitle: Methodology for Forecasting the Power Production of PV Plants During Solar Eclipse
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: On July 2, 2019, a total solar eclipse occurred in the southern part of South America. This affected mainly the electrical systems of; Chile, Argentina, Peru, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Brazil. Considering this type of events, this research proposes a procedure that allows predicting the energy production of an industrial size photovoltaic plant under conditions of high variation of solar irradiance. The methodology is broken down into two stages: in the first, a heuristic methodology is developed to forecast irradiance, while in the second, supervised learning machines are used to estimate the production of photovoltaic plants. The results show that the overall error is of the order of 21%, which were contrasted with the measurements obtained during the eclipse of 2 July.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Synthesis Through Genetic Algorithms for Urban V2V Communications: Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: This paper presents preliminary results regarding the use of genetic algorithms (GA) to improve V2V communications in urban intersections. The work considers the principles of the IEEE 802.11p standard, and looks to improve the range of communication for V2V communications in urban intersections by making the GA learn beam shapes according to the surrounding environment. Preliminary results show that with the same power as an isotropic antenna, the GA is able to improve the power in all relevant directions, which should result in increasing the communication range.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Stochastic Gradient MCMC using Multi-Core and GPU Architectures
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: Deep learning models are traditionally used in big data scenarios. When there is not enough training data to fit a large model, transfer learning re-purpose the learned features from an existing model and re-train the lower layers for the new task. Bayesian inference techniques can be used to capture the uncertainty of the new model but it comes with a high computational cost. In this paper, the run time performance of an Stochastic Gradient Markov Chain Monte Carlo method using two different architectures is compared, namely GPU and multi-core CPU. As opposed to the widely usage of GPUs for deep learning, significant advantages from using modern CPU architectures.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a sensor array for navigation in a dynamic environment in an eight degrees-of-freedom omnidirectional vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: Robot navigation trough dynamics environments is a complex task that is both time consuming and highly computational intense. In this paper, it is studied the usage of low power and low complexity sensors mounted in an 8 degrees of freedom mini autonomous vehicle applied to the navigation trough a dynamic scenery. Using a TSP-based modification to the classical A* navigation algorithm for the path planning stage, the 3 proposed systems initially work alone where they are evaluated, and further on, implemented as an integrated system. In this respect, the aim of this experiment, made in conjunction of MATLAB and V-REP, is to compare different sensors arrays in many case studies, discuss the behavior and the performance to further selection of them.

articleTitle: Space-Heating Replacement Scenarios, From Biomass to Electricity: A Case Study in Valdivia
publicationTitle: 2020 Congreso Estudiantil de Electrónica y Electricidad (INGELECTRA)
abstract: The residential sector in Valdivia, Chile, is responsible for 94.1% of fine particle-matter (PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub>) emissions due to wood-based stoves for space heating. Consequently, in 2017 a local Atmospheric Decontamination Plan (ADP) defined goals that have been difficult to achieve. The purpose of this work is to show the effect on the emissions of PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> when replacing the wood-based heating systems by electric space-heating with a horizon up to 2030. This is done by defining and comparing five scenarios based on the current public policies and 2 of electric-heating replacement. The study also shows the increase of the electricity demand in the zone, in the electric-heating scenarios. We find that the scenario with the largest impact is related to the appropriate use of the stoves, even before replacing them for electric air-conditioning systems. However, this scenario has shown to be difficult to be implemented in practice. The electric-heating replacement scenarios show that with a minimum rate of 742 changes per year, the emissions of PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> start being reduced by 2030, while the energy consumption is increased in 27'556 MWh/year, representing an 8% of the overall electricity consumption in the city by 2030.
